subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: After the propagation defects are fixed, should `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` remain model-visible on unauthorized turns while immutable turn grants enforce authority only immediately before execution?
rationale: Source inspection supports the gate structure, but choosing tool-schema visibility as the permanent security and caching contract requires explicit maintainer intent and live boundary proof.

options.title: Keep visible schemas with hard gates
options.body: Retain the stable catalogue only after exact-head proof shows denied calls stop before hooks and side effects while owner and trusted-internal calls still execute.

options.title: Preserve inventory filtering
options.body: Keep protected schemas absent on unauthorized turns and pursue a narrower cache-stability mechanism that does not change visibility.

recommendation.title: Keep visible schemas with hard gates
recommendation.body: Retain the stable catalogue only after exact-head proof shows denied calls stop before hooks and side effects while owner and trusted-internal calls still execute.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the overlapping immutable CLI/MCP grant, revocation, and execution-authority boundary on current main.
